name: Hamilton Microlab STAR
status_line: In PyLabRobot. The real STARDriver sends text firmware commands over USB.
reaches: USB, VID 0x08AF, PID 0x8000 (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/master.py:81-82). The host speaks first: ASCII commands like C0TPid0117xp... Each reply repeats module, command and id, then er00/00 or an error code (pylabrobot/hamilton/protocol/text/framing.py:3-5 and pylabrobot/hamilton/protocol/text/framing.py:319-320).
decoded_from: Upstream does not say how the commands were first obtained. Its code cites the firmware docs (pylabrobot/hamilton/protocol/text/framing.py:38), marks some codes as observed, not documented (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/errors.py:349), and its debug page compares PLR commands with VENUS USB trace files (docs/user_guide/hamilton/star/debug.md:7-11).
steps: With Python 3.10 or newer, in a virtual environment: pip install "pylabrobot[usb]", which adds pyusb and libusb-package (docs/user_guide/getting-started/installation.md:3 and docs/user_guide/getting-started/installation.md:47).
Connect the STAR by its USB cable. On macOS also install libusb (brew install libusb); on Linux the docs list nothing more (docs/user_guide/getting-started/installation.md:90-100).

On Windows, with no Hamilton or VENUS software running, use Zadig to give "ML Star" the libusbK driver; restore the original driver for VENUS (docs/user_guide/getting-started/installation.md:108-144).
STARDriver() with no io opens the USB device itself, VID 0x08AF, PID 0x8000 (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/master.py:145-152).
Build the deck as it stands, then star = STARlet(deck=deck) or STAR(deck=deck). Setup refuses a deck whose track count differs from the device's (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/master.py:1155-1171).
await star.setup() reads the device, then initializes it, so it moves (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/master.py:214). Then a first small step, such as picking up tips.
scenario: Start-up conversation, then pick up 8 tips, aspirate 50 uL from column 1 of a source plate, dispense into column 1 of a destination plate, return the tips. Volumes made up.
real: pylabrobot STARDriver, STARlet device and Pipettes feature, unchanged
Every frame the driver wrote: 274 commands; the log shows 7 kinds
Upstream liquid class: 50 uL asked goes out as av00551, 55.1 uL
simulated: The USB transport, every reply and the reply router's clock (sim.py)
Device state: tips per channel, liquid per tip, volume per well
A cut-down STARlet: 8 channels, no iSWAP, 96-head or autoload
not_checked: Nothing ran on a physical STAR
Reply values and padding beyond the upstream recording and test captures
Timing, motion, real liquid behaviour and real error codes for this move
limits: The device registry still points STAR at the legacy STARBackend, api v0 (docs/_static/devices.json:539-540).

Only the STAR recording was read off a device; the STARlet and STARplus ones are derived (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/recordings/README.md:5-7 and pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/recordings/README.md:47).

50 uL becomes 55.1 uL: the 400 uL tip maps to the 300 uL water class StandardVolume_Water_DispenseSurface_Part, curve 50.0: 55.1 (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/liquid_classes/mapping.py:46 and pylabrobot/hamilton/star/liquid_classes/mapping.py:14004-14010).
Upstream's own STARSimulationDriver answers above the wire: nothing reaches it (pylabrobot/hamilton/star/driver/simulator.py:8), so wire replies here are this example's.
